% \pixdiamond{x}{y}{cell}{inner}{outer}{colour}: pixel diamond centred on (x,y); fills cells with
% inner <= |i|+|j| <= outer (inner=outer: thin ring; inner<outer: thick ring, hollow centre).
\newcommand{\pixdiamond}[6]{%
  \foreach \i in {-#5,...,#5}{\foreach \j in {-#5,...,#5}{%
    \pgfmathtruncatemacro{\d}{abs(\i)+abs(\j)}%
    \ifnum\d<#4\relax\else\ifnum\d>#5\relax\else
      \fill[#6!\pixopacity!softwhite] ($(#1,#2)+(\i*#3-#3/2,\j*#3-#3/2)$) rectangle +(#3,#3);
    \fi\fi}}}
% \legobrick{x}{y}{cell}{colour}{two|four|six}: one 2x2, 2x4 or 2x6 brick, origin at (x,y).
% Each face shade is pre-mixed with the page colour, so bricks are drawn solid and overlap correctly.
\newcommand{\legobrick}[5]{%
  \expandafter\let\expandafter\legocur\csname lego#5top\endcsname
  \foreach \i/\j/\n in \legocur
    \fill[#4!50!white!\pixopacity!softwhite] ($(#1,#2)+(\i*#3,\j*#3)$) rectangle +(\n*#3,#3);
  \expandafter\let\expandafter\legocur\csname lego#5left\endcsname
  \foreach \i/\j/\n in \legocur
    \fill[#4!\pixopacity!softwhite] ($(#1,#2)+(\i*#3,\j*#3)$) rectangle +(\n*#3,#3);
  \expandafter\let\expandafter\legocur\csname lego#5right\endcsname
  \foreach \i/\j/\n in \legocur
    \fill[#4!65!black!\pixopacity!softwhite] ($(#1,#2)+(\i*#3,\j*#3)$) rectangle +(\n*#3,#3);
  \expandafter\let\expandafter\legocur\csname lego#5studside\endcsname
  \foreach \i/\j/\n in \legocur
    \fill[#4!85!black!\pixopacity!softwhite] ($(#1,#2)+(\i*#3,\j*#3)$) rectangle +(\n*#3,#3);
  \expandafter\let\expandafter\legocur\csname lego#5studtop\endcsname
  \foreach \i/\j/\n in \legocur
    \fill[#4!35!white!\pixopacity!softwhite] ($(#1,#2)+(\i*#3,\j*#3)$) rectangle +(\n*#3,#3);}

% Every logo gets the same box: scaled to fit (aspect ratio kept), then padded
% on the right and centred vertically on the text, so marks of different shapes
% occupy identical space.
\newlength{\logoboxw}\setlength{\logoboxw}{1.4em}
\newlength{\logoboxh}\setlength{\logoboxh}{1.0em}
% Entry title linked to the organisation's site, styled as a conventional
% hyperlink: no link box, text and underline in the section-heading blue
% (accentblue). The logo links too but sits outside the underline.
% Usage: \entrytitle[logo opts]{logo}{url}{text};  \bluelink{url}{text} inline.
\newcommand{\bluelink}[2]{{\hypersetup{pdfborder={0 0 0}}\href{#1}{{\color{accentblue}\underline{#2}}}}}
\newcommand{\entrytitle}[4][]{{%
  \hypersetup{pdfborder={0 0 0}}%
  \href{#3}{\complogo[#1]{#2}}%
  \bluelink{#3}{#4}}}
\newcommand{\complogo}[2][]{%
  \makebox[\logoboxw][l]{\raisebox{\dimexpr0.35em-\height/2\relax}{%
    \includegraphics[width=\logoboxw,height=\logoboxh,keepaspectratio,#1]{logos/#2}}}%
  \hspace{0.3em}}

% Override frcontent so body (#3) can hold complex content like \begin{itemize}.
% Emit a line break BEFORE each non-empty field (not after) so items that omit
% the trailing field (#4) don't leave a dangling \newline and produce uneven
% vertical spacing between list items.
\makeatletter
\renewenvironment{frcontent}[4]{%
  {%
    \textbf{#1}%
    {\footnotesize
      \def\@frcarg{#2}\ifx\@frcarg\@empty\else{\leavevmode\newline #2}\fi
      \def\@frcarg{#3}\ifx\@frcarg\@empty\else{\leavevmode\newline #3}\fi
      \def\@frcarg{#4}\ifx\@frcarg\@empty\else{\leavevmode\newline\textit{#4}}\fi
    }%
  }%
}{}
\makeatother

						\item \frcontent{\bluelink{https://iteksi.com}{iTeksi!}: visibility for Cape Town's minibus taxi network}{}{As a team of 3 we built iTeksi! at the Builders' Table. Cape Town's 830\,000 daily taxi trips are invisible: can we change that to improve South Africa's transport network? Our approach: digitise demand and resolve information asymmetry while minimising change management. Drivers get simple, bold actions that measure what already happens; riders have one proactive signal, a ping showing where they are and where they want to go. Together these feed an insightful dashboard for owners, the persona we sell to: demand by route, vehicle activity and, above all, live earnings. My favourite feature: pay-as-you-go credits redeemed by the driver's QR scan, so vulnerable passengers don't carry cash.}{Built on the Alis Exchange platform}
						\item \frcontent{Blueprint: A recursive multi-agent system for decomposing concepts into components of a technology stack}{}{A deterministic orchestrator recursively invokes three specialised LLM agents --- \textit{concept-to-component}, \textit{concept-decomposer}, and \textit{technologist} --- which together break a high-level software concept into sub-concepts and map each to a component of a recommended technology stack. The orchestrator itself gates termination via confidence scores on every mapping: either the blueprint is returned or decomposition continues. I am testing the hypothesis that replacing broad task management with a confidence-gated recursive loop over narrow agents lets LLMs handle requests whose scope would otherwise overwhelm a single model.
						      }{Go, A2A, ADK, gRPC, Gemini, Flutter}
